source_text: Hae uisiones insigniores ipsorum martyrum beatissimorum Saturi et Perpetuae, quas ipsi conscripserunt. Secundulum uero deus maturiore exitu de saeculo adhuc in carcere euocauit, non sine gratia, ut bestias lucraretur. Gladium tamen etsi non anima, certe caro eius agnouit.
pass_a_gloss: These are the more distinguished visions of the most blessed martyrs Saturus and Perpetua themselves, which they themselves wrote out. But as for Secundulus, God called him forth from the world while still in prison by a more timely departure, not without favor, with the result that he gained exemption from the beasts. Nevertheless, even if his soul did not, his flesh certainly experienced the sword.
pass_b_english: These are the signal visions of the most blessed martyrs Saturus and Perpetua, which they themselves set down in writing. As for Secundulus, God summoned him from this world while he was still in prison by an earlier death, not without grace, sparing him the beasts. Yet though his soul did not meet it, his flesh certainly came to know the sword.

lemmas.gloss: visions seen in sleep or ecstasy
by an earlier or timely departure, that is death
from the world, from present life

choices.why: ablative of means with comparative maturiore marking Secundulus dying before the arena, not merely a timely death in general
subjunctive of result after non sine gratia; lucror with object bestias here means profit by escaping them, i.e. death in prison exempted him from the arena
rejected: that he might win the beasts

choices.term: etsi non anima, certe caro eius
choices.english: even if his soul did not, his flesh certainly did
choices.why: concessive etsi with ellipsis of agnouit after anima; caro versus anima contrasts bodily suffering with the soul spared the arena
rejected: although not in soul, yet in his flesh
